problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\frac{3+4x}{2-3x}$ and the point $P(1,-7)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(-7,1).$

feedback.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(8,6).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =3\sqrt[3]{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =3\cdot \frac{1}{3}{x}^{-2/3} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}} \\ {f}^{′}(8) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{{8}^{2}}} \\ {f}^{′}(8) & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(8,6)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(6,8)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(6) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(6))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(8)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
